done.why: I died to the troll, woke in the forest empty-handed, climbed a tree and saw the egg, then stopped. I had not explored fully.

about: A close retelling of Zork. You start at the white house, take the lantern, sword and sack, and go down into the cellar. A troll that answers back guards the way and kills careless players.

ending.what: No ending. I died to the troll and was returned to the forest.

moments.note: The kitchen is vivid. The sack smells of hot peppers, and the bottle's contents are listed.
The trap door crashes shut as I go down, and I hear someone barring it. Unsettling and fitting.
Giving the sack to the troll got a funny reply, then an axe hit.
I was told I was still recovering from a blow, then I died. There was little chance to react.
The jeweled egg in the nest is described with real care.

wished: Some warning that the troll could kill me so fast.
A way to read the leaflet or other things again without retaking them.
More time to see the rest of the map.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: A short line that adds menace and an unseen presence.

lines.line: The troll, who is not overly proud, graciously accepts the gift and not having the most discriminating tastes, gleefully eats it.
Unlike most eggs, this one is hinged and closed with a delicate looking clasp.

fun.why: Familiar and pleasant, but I died early and saw little.

engagement.why: The prose pulled me in, but I stopped after a short session.

difficulty.why: The troll killed me in three turns, with no warning and no real way to respond.

interestingness.why: It is mostly the classic game. The troll's replies were the one thing I saw that felt new.

prose.why: Clean, witty and well observed, with small details like the pepper smell and the egg's clasp.
